themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 13 this week, a 76% increase over the 8-week baseline average of 7.4 complaints per week, suggesting an emerging pest control crisis in East Harlem requiring immediate investigation into causes and city response.
evidence: 13 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.26, 76% increase)
Spike occurred in isolation—not part of broader seasonal pattern given stable baseline
Aligns with district's ongoing budget request for graffiti removal/sanitation improvements, suggesting chronic infrastructure gaps
reporting_angles: Interview residents in blocks with concentrated complaints; visit homes to document conditions
Contact DOHMH and Sanitation to understand response time and resource allocation to East Harlem
Investigate whether recent construction activity (564 DOB filings, including 75 new buildings) has disrupted waste management or created new harborage

themes_detail.label: Garbage Collection Failures
themes_detail.summary: Missed collection complaints jumped to 9 this week, a 227% spike over the 8-week average of 2.8 weekly complaints, indicating a sudden sanitation service breakdown affecting waste management in the district.
evidence: 9 missed collection complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.74, 227% increase)
Spike is acute and recent; no prior spike in this complaint category in the 90-day dataset
Complements 713 unsanitary condition complaints (90-day total), suggesting compounding sanitation crisis
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Sanitation to identify whether East Harlem routes are understaffed, vehicle breakdowns, or scheduling errors
Map missed collections geographically; interview residents on affected blocks about how long waste has accumulated
Cross-check with Rodent complaint locations—does missed collection precede rodent spikes on same blocks?

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints surged to 124 last week, a 54% increase over the 8-week baseline of 80.6 weekly complaints (z-score: 3.78), becoming the third-highest complaint type overall and pointing to possible enforcement gaps or new parking demand.
evidence: 124 illegal parking complaints last week vs. 80.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (54% increase, z-score: 3.78)
Blocked driveway complaints also up 74% last week (15 vs. 8.6 avg), suggesting related phenomena
Community board has repeatedly requested additional traffic enforcement agents, signaling chronic enforcement resource gap
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD Traffic Enforcement to understand staffing levels and deployment strategy in CD 111
Survey residents and businesses on 125th Street corridor about parking availability and enforcement visibility
Examine whether 58-62 East 125th Street rezoning (currently in review) has altered parking demand or supply in the area

themes_detail.label: Park Rules Violations Spike
themes_detail.summary: Park rules violation complaints jumped to 4 this week, a 433% increase over the 8-week average of 0.8 weekly complaints, indicating a sudden shift in park usage or policing patterns requiring urgent clarification.
evidence: 4 park rules violation complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 2.5, 433% increase)
This is a newly emergent complaint type with extreme baseline volatility, requiring context on which parks and which violations
Community board's standing budget request for 'park, building, or access improvements' suggests parks infrastructure has been a concern
reporting_angles: Identify which parks generated complaints; interview Parks Dept about enforcement changes or increased patrols
Visit parks to observe conditions and speak with regular users about recent changes in activity or enforcement
Determine whether violations relate to homeless encampments, substance use, vandalism, or other categories

themes_detail.label: Elevator Outages in Rental Housing
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints spiked to 4 about 3 weeks ago, a 433% increase over the 8-week baseline of 0.8 complaints, suggesting possible failures in multi-unit residential buildings affecting mobility and accessibility for residents.
evidence: 4 elevator complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 3.36, 433% increase)
Spike occurred 3 weeks ago; no follow-up spikes in current week suggest either resolution or under-reporting
Converges with 1,686 heat/hot water complaints and 511 plumbing complaints, pointing to broader building maintenance failures
reporting_angles: Identify buildings with elevator outages and investigate building ownership, maintenance records, and 311 response times
Interview elderly and disabled residents about impacts of prolonged outages on access to homes and services
Cross-reference DOB permits: were any of the 75 new buildings or 466 alterations on these blocks incomplete or causing infrastructure disruptions?
